text:
[IRET.9.5] **Evaluation order.** `and` / `or` may evaluate their operands
in any order and may stop once the result is decided, but the result must be
[LNUL.4.2]'s absorbing one. An operand that faults — a trap, a `TypeError`, or
an `EngineError` raised by evaluating it — does not end the evaluation: the
evaluator holds the fault, evaluates the remaining operands, and a `false`
(`true` for `or`) among them decides the result and discards every held fault.
When nothing decides, the expression yields the one fault [LNUL.4.2]'s order
selects. A held fault that is discarded or not selected reaches no fault
surface ([LERR.1.4.11]).

alloy.name: iret_9_5__evaluated
alloy.note: What the rest evaluated: up to and including the stop, or all of it. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: iret_9_5__ord
alloy.note: The orders the conjuncts may be evaluated in, one atom each.

alloy.name: iret_9_5__orders
alloy.note: Each a strict total order, no two alike: with six atoms every order is present.

alloy.name: iret_9_5__stop
alloy.note: The first false of the rest in the order -- the only thing V5 stops at. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

alloy.name: iret_9_5__v5_order_independent
alloy.note: ORDER INDEPENDENCE: every order gives one answer and records one atom, over every `where` of up to three conjuncts. A positional pick breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and
idris.note: The result of and is the absorbing one, whatever the order of evaluation: A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and_commutes
idris.note: Any order of evaluation gives the same and: a trapping operand does not end it, and a false elsewhere decides.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__or
idris.note: The result of or is the absorbing one, whatever the order of evaluation: A TRAP IS ABSORBED ([LERR.1.4.1]): a false (for or, a true) on either side decides; otherwise a trap on either side is raised; otherwise Kleene's table.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__trap_absorbed
idris.note: An operand that traps does not end the evaluation: a false (for or, a true) in the other operand decides the result.

idris.name: Iret_9_5__perm
idris.note: One list a reordering of another.

idris.name: iret_9_5__any_order
idris.note: Evaluating ANY reordering of the source, left to right and stopping at a false, gives the `where`'s answer and records its fault. [LERR.1.4.11]: only the fault the expression yields reaches a surface -- recorded ([RFCS.21.1]), delivered to a callback or counted -- and the model's record stands for all three. Recording every evaluated fault (M2) is not order independent (`gap__m2_order_dependent`, a counterexample tied to no clause). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: iret_9_5__perm_refl
idris.note: Every list is a reordering of itself.

idris.name: iret_9_5__seq
idris.note: Evaluation left to right, stopping at the first false: [IRET.9.5]'s evaluator holds a fault, evaluates the remaining operands, and a false among them decides and discards every held fault. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: iret_9_5__seq_v5
idris.note: Stopping at the first false loses nothing: the evaluation is the answer. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__and5
idris.note: The V5 `and`. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: lnul_4_2__v5_perm
idris.note: ORDER INDEPENDENCE: a `where`'s V5 answer does not depend on the order of its conjuncts -- [IRET.7.6]'s join tests 'may be evaluated in any order'. V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: rfcs_21_1__pair_record_order_free
idris.note: A PAIR'S RECORD IS A FUNCTION OF THE PAIR, however its conjuncts are ordered or evaluated: what the trap record needs to be a function of the join relation, and [IRET.7.6]'s 'the pair yields the one fault [LNUL.4.2]'s order selects'. [LERR.1.4.11]: only the fault the expression yields reaches a surface -- recorded ([RFCS.21.1]), delivered to a callback or counted -- and the model's record stands for all three. Recording every evaluated fault (M2) is not order independent (`gap__m2_order_dependent`, a counterexample tied to no clause). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.
